paragraphs.text: DSH control center for locally installed Codex and Claude Code
# dsh-coding-agents
**Drive your local Codex and Claude Code from DeepSeek Harness — sessions, config and run state, fro
m one settings page and six agent tools.**
English | 中文
The plugin calls the public, stable local interfaces of Codex and Claude Code. It never parses or re
writes their private databases, and every write goes through the vendor's own configuration protocol
or a backup-plus-atomic-replace.

## Use your own Codex & Claude Code
The plugin never pins a vendor version. Each engine resolves independently, in order: `config.codexC
ommand` / `config.claudeCommand` → system `PATH` (`codex` / `claude`) → the CLI bundled in this pack
age → unavailable with an actionable message. The status page reports the source (`config` / `system
` / `bundled`) and the version read from `<cli> --version`.
- **Global install:** install Codex / Claude Code normally (e.g. `npm i -g @openai/codex`); the plug

in drives the CLI already on your `PATH`, including future upgrades.
- **Install it in this profile:
** `dsh plugin --profile <name> add @openai/codex` (or `pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) —

both are *optional peers*, so the plugin never dictates your version.

## What you can do
- Search the local session history of both Codex and Claude Code, and page through very long transcr

ipts.
- Start, continue or fork a native session, watch text, tool calls and run state live, and can

cel a run.
- Rename, tag, archive, unarchive, roll back and delete sessions. Operations that do not

apply to an engine are refused explicitly instead of failing silently.
- Inspect configuration value
s, their effective values and their origin. Codex writes through its official config protocol; Claud

e Code uses backup plus atomic replace.
- The same capabilities are exposed to the DSH agent as six
`coding_agent_*` tools, not only through the settings page.
## Natural-language examples

- "List the most recent Codex and Claude Code sessions."
- "Find the history that mentions the login

failure."
- "Continue that Codex session and run the tests."
- "Start a Claude Code task in this wo

rkspace and fix the build error."
- "Read the current Codex configuration."
The plugin only drives engines that the current user has installed and logged in. Runs default to wo
rkspace-write permissions, and full access is never reachable from a web page or from a model tool:
it only happens when you start the run yourself in the DSH UI.
## Safety boundaries
- **Loopback + same-origin HTTP only.** `/coding-agents-api` rejects any request whose TCP peer is n
ot this machine (403), any browser request whose `Origin` is not exactly the `http://<host>` it was
sent to (403), any request whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site` (403), every POST without `content
-type: application/json` (415), and CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`, 405). A random web page therefore can
not drive your local Codex or Claude Code, even with a "simple" request that skips the CORS prefligh

t.
- **No full access through HTTP.** The HTTP surface accepts only `read-only` and `workspace-write
`; `full-access` (Claude Code `bypassPermissions`, Codex `danger-full-access`) is reachable only fro
m the DSH UI, where you confirm it yourself. The model tools mirror this ceiling: `coding_agent_run`

refuses `full-access` with an actionable error.
- **Registered workspaces bound every `cwd`.** A `c
wd` is accepted only when it resolves inside a workspace registered in DSH; paths are normalised and
traversal outside a registered root is refused. When the host exposes no workspace registry, reques

ts carrying a `cwd` are refused instead of trusting the caller.
- **Configuration writes are allowli
sted.** HTTP may write only `model` and `model_reasoning_effort` (Codex) or `permissions.defaultMode
` (Claude Code). Every other key — MCP servers, hooks, permission presets, arbitrary nesting — needs
the DSH UI or a manual edit. Both engines back the file up before a write (Claude Code: backup + at
omic replace; Codex: `config.toml.backup-dsh-<timestamp>` before its official config protocol write)

.
- No vendor private database is read; only the public local interfaces.
- Child processes live in

the host's `subprocess` service and inherit a scrubbed environment (`scrubbedParentEnv`).
- Session
operations stay scoped to the workspace that owns the session.

## Known limitations
- Requires a local Codex / Claude Code installation and login. Without it the engine reports an expl

icit unavailable state.
- Native executables are resolved on first use. If a package manager skipped
the platform optional dependency, only that engine reports an actionable "unavailable" state (statu
s page, `coding_agent_status`, run start) while the plugin itself still imports and the other engine

keeps working; reinstall with optional dependencies enabled to restore it.
- The bundled CLI fallba
ck (when present) is large, so the first install depends on network speed; using your own global CLI

avoids it entirely.
- The HTTP API is a loopback `http://` surface by design: a TLS or non-loopback

DSH web deployment is refused rather than downgraded.
- The plugin drives the vendor CLIs; it does
not reimplement their agent loops.
